Extend the simplex-lattice scan to higher dimensions (d up to 30) by checking the real maximum element (n·B^(d-1) ≤ 1e15) instead of the loose B^d < 1e14 bound, restrict to larger sets, and evaluate the largest sets first under a time guard.

I extended the simplex-lattice scan to also try capped simplices (coordinates ≤ m, sum ≤ n), using base 2m+1. It scans candidates with 1500–4000 points, simplex shapes first, under a time guard, and keeps the best exact score.

I'm adding a hill-climb over the integer embedding weights (not just base 2n+1).
